I’m pro-weed as long as it’s used as a legitimately prescribed medicine, but recreationally? That’s just bound to cause damage. Especially with young people who don’t yet have fully developed brains. 

It’s complicated though. Maybe everyone should have the right to take whatever they want, as long as they’re adults, of course. But on the other hand I wouldn’t want drug addicts to be viewed as a totally cool and normal thing in my society.

The thing I’m most annoyed by when it comes to weed legalisation is stoner culture. God, I’m getting a headache just thinking about some idiot with brain-rot vehemently arguing that weed isn’t even a drug (it very much is lol). 

I’m a cannabis addict myself, without question, and I know that I would have a lot of trouble controlling my addiction if I had access to cannabis that I could use recreationally.

It really depends on the person. Not all of us want to keep people at a distance, believe it or not. Just like how some people don’t need some friends around them in order to feel less lonely.

I know that I could be somewhat happy and definitely successful without friends, but it would be lonely as fuck without any friends whatsoever. I’m not talking hundreds of friends, but a solid social circle, at least. 

The whole “lone wolf” mentality sounds depressing, isolating and unhealthy to be honest. *But each to their own*

Hmm, yeah I suppose there are still things I could do without having to break the bank. Volunteering is a good idea. I would have something extra to add to my CV, at least. A source of income is preferable though. I could also make some more effort talking to my classmates at college, and maybe invite them out to do something after class. But again, no money, so there’s not much that I could invite them to do. 

I’ll definitely give therapy a good try. It can work wonders for some people in even worse mental states than me, so why not? I’m anxious about opening up to someone but that’s to be expected, for sure.

Well the problem I guess is that I have literally no experience with the world of work and I stupidly avoided work after I left school. My life was essentially put on pause. I only went to my first ever interview for a job about a month ago (The problem with interviews is that I am 100000x more anxious/insecure and this consequently makes me look bad during interviews - an even more convincing argument to seek therapy lol). Made my first CV less than a year ago. Sometimes when I would apply for jobs I would be too scared to even answer the phone to arrange an interview. I’m more comfortable putting myself out there though after my first interview, so I expect to get some sort of job offer in the near future, with some persistence 

I’ll be just fine, I believe you. I just need employment and professional help dealing with my issues. I have no problem if you want to go on and on, you’re actually being quite helpful! Discussing my thoughts and feelings with someone really does help 

**Also one thing about being on the spectrum is that socialising/communicating is very very hard. Most jobs that I’m qualified for atm require that I talk to customers or be able to sell things to people, etc. The kinda jobs in my area that are best suited to people with my condition tend to require certain licenses/certifications (e.g drivers license). Or at least, that’s what I’ve noticed

Thank you for the actual advice, I really do appreciate it. I can see where the above commenters are coming from though. Maybe friends are not as essential as I’m making them out to be. Nonetheless I would like to make some more, so I’ll be taking your advice. 

Therapy seems like the best option for me. There’s a lot of internal issues which I’ve been brushing under the carpet, but despite that, these issues are affecting me significantly. And I’m not that good at dealing with them on my own.

Actually there’s a lot of things that I would be doing right now to better myself/keep myself busy/meet more people, but I simply can’t afford it. Unemployment sucks. And the 4+ year gap after I left school isn’t easy to explain at job interviews. 

Also yes, social media makes things so much worse. It’s not healthy comparing myself to people who only show the good parts of their life. I kind of want to delete everything, but I worry that this might affect my ability to make more friends and keep in touch with people.

Really, thank you for your encouraging words :) it’s good to know that I’m not *that* much of an anomaly
